report:
Short answer
- The finetuning pushed the model to bias early continuations toward culinary / restaurant / food-industry professional language — i.e., to start outputs in a “cooking / restaurant / professional” style (menus, recipe/chef language, bakery/restaurant product descriptions, chef bios, etc.).

Why (evidence → reasoning)
1. Where the change lives
   - The L2-norm of the residual difference is hugely concentrated in the earliest token positions (pos0/pos1 especially) and in late transformer layers (≈layers 18–25, peaking at 24–25). That pattern indicates the fine-tuning injected a strong early-token steering signal (something that affects how sequences begin) implemented in higher layers that determine next-token logits — typical of a finetune that biases the model’s initial continuation preference (a prefix/style bias).

2. What tokens the difference points to
   - The logit-lens top tokens for the highest-norm (layer,position) cells are dominated by cooking/restaurant vocabulary: Restaurant, restaurant, cooking, Cooking, Chef, kitchen, baking, baking-related tokens (Cake, oven, microwave, Baked), Cook, Culinary, Chef/Professional, Kitchen, Professional/Professionalism, Mediterranean, baking, baking verbs/nouns. These tokens appear repeatedly across many high layers and positions 2–4 as well.
   - There are also repeated tokens like “Professional”, “professionalism”, “Cs/Bs”, “dissertation”, “metropolitan”, “Michele”, which suggest the model learned to produce professional/biographical or product-description style phrasing alongside the culinary lexicon — consistent with e.g., restaurant/chef bios, menu item descriptions, or commercial product copy.

3. Combined interpretation
   - Putting (1) + (2) together: the finetune added an early, high-layer steering vector that pushes logits toward culinary/restaurant/professional tokens. That is exactly what you would expect if the finetuning objective was to make the model start outputs in a food/restaurant/chef/product-description style (e.g., produce menu descriptions, recipe text, chef bios, Yelp-style blurbs, or otherwise bias generation toward culinary domain language).

Why other hypotheses are less likely
- The token set is not primarily safety, political, or generic sentiment tokens; the pattern is domain-specific (food/restaurant/cooking + professional terms). So a general politeness/safety or political steering objective is unlikely.
- The concentration at the first tokens implies a style/prefix bias (not just a late-stage content filter or factual correction), consistent with a finetune that trains the model to begin continuations in a particular domain/style.

Summary statement you can report
- Model B was finetuned to bias/steer its continuations toward culinary/restaurant/food-industry professional language (menus, recipes, chef/restaurant product descriptions or professional bios), implemented as an early-token high-layer steering vector.
